question: On the already declared correlated K times Lambda strip, does the selected real plus-recessive family have a uniform strictly negative projective kappa sensitivity h=partial_kappa rho at Qplus=4?
primary_sources: NIST DLMF section 2.7(iii), Liouville-Green approximation: https://dlmf.nist.gov/2.7#iii

declared_conventions.selected_family: the same real plus-recessive family selected and linked on the certified correlated sign strip; h is invariant under a nonzero kappa-dependent common amplitude
declared_conventions.two_parameter_secant: at fixed lambda and for kappa_a<kappa_b, [r_b(4)-r_a(4)]/[kappa_b-kappa_a]=-(kappa_a+kappa_b)*integral_4^infinity v_a(Q)*v_b(Q) dQ
declared_conventions.derivative_scope: two-sided partial_kappa derivative at every corridor-interior kappa and the corresponding one-sided derivative at each kappa face, uniformly for lambda in the closed slab
declared_conventions.plus_log_derivative_envelope: 53*exp(Q)<=r=-u_Q/u<=70*exp(Q) for Q>=4 on the full declared strip

integral_bounds.definition: I_ab=integral_4^infinity v_a(Q)*v_b(Q) dQ; I_kk=u_kappa(4)^(-2)*integral_4^infinity u_kappa(Q)^2 dQ

declared_conventions.execution: exact SymPy identities and rational inequalities only; no Arb evaluation, Bessel call, ODE solve, quadrature, root solve, finite difference, sampling, panel transport or bisection

upstream_results.role: pins the selected real plus-recessive construction and its full Q>=4, abs(lambda)<=1e-4, 0<=kappa<=8 Liouville-Green error bound
pins the exact current K times Lambda scope, the selected actual-family linkage, and the already audited full-strip plus log-derivative envelope; it does not supply a kappa derivative

assumptions: For every point of the compact declared strip, the hash-pinned sign-strip result supplies the same selected real plus-recessive direction and the executable full-strip derivation of 53*exp(Q)<=-u_Q/u<=70*exp(Q). No face difference or root result is used to infer a derivative.

Parameter differentiability at Qplus is not assumed: at each fixed lambda, the two-parameter Wronskian secant identity first gives finite-Q local Lipschitz continuity in kappa; normalized-direction convergence and uniform tail domination then give both diagonal limits by dominated convergence.
The elementary integral bounds deliberately sacrifice sharpness. They are sufficient only to establish a finite strictly negative Qplus kappa-sensitivity interval.
This endpoint anchor alone does not transport h to Qswitch or Q0 and does not evaluate partial_kappa G, prove root uniqueness, construct a selector, or determine root velocity.
